ravi: Quick triage — noticed a production perf regression affecting qwen2.5 today after the runtime kernel-routing change. p95 latency jumped ~95% for multilingual prompts and KV cache hit-rate fell from ~92% to ~63%. Leaving logs here, need heads-up and quick hypothesis.

alex: grabbing profiler output now. flamegraph uploaded: https://infralogs/internal/flame/1834123456. Early look: a lot more time in tokenization + memcpy during prefill. KV lookup appears to be doing extra copies.

sarah: hypothesis: kernel selector heuristic started preferring the small-seq kernel for some batch shapes after the rope-scaling tweak we merged. small-seq path has a different KV layout (kv_head_dim packing) which could desync if tokenizer boundaries change between languages.

jen: adding another datapoint — repro with zh+en prompt shows token counts differ by 1 vs baseline tokenizer normalization. e.g. baseline tokenization of the same Unicode string produced 21 tokens, new tokenizer pipeline produced 22. That off-by-one can shift RoPE positions and cause cache indexing differences.

alex: profiler snippet: ```
# perf top sample
prefill_tokenize  38.2%  runtime
kv_cache_lookup   24.5%  runtime
small_seq_kernel_dispatch 18.0% runtime
memcpy            11.3%  runtime
other             8.0%
```

alex: quick A/B: forcing kernel_selector.override=large_seq for qwen2.5 in canary reduced p95 back to ~200ms (from 340ms) and restored KV hit-rate to ~90%. So kernel path seems tightly coupled with tokenizer output assumptions.

ravi: ok — two angles: 1) tokenizer normalization/regression (multilang) that changes token boundaries, 2) kernel path mismatch (kv packing/head dims) when switching to small_seq. Both could combine to break KV index invariants.

jen: reproducer I ran locally: input = "混合 language test — emoji 👍". Baseline tokenization: ["混","合"," language"," test"," —"," emoji"," 👍"] (7 tokens). New pipeline: ["混","合","  la","nguage"," test"," —"," emoji"," 👍"] (8 tokens). So internal byte-alignment changed.

sarah: that reproducer is 🔑. Suggest we add a deterministic token-count assertion into the runtime prefill code for qwen2.5 (fail early and log tokenization diffs) while we bisect tokenizer changes. Also need to add a kernel-selector safety check: if selected kernel expects kv_head_dim==attention_head_dim * factor, assert and fallback.

infra-bot: deploy: rolled back runtime change 2026-11-02T23:41:12Z — triggered by perf-alerts. Canary = previous build.

alex: after rollback numbers look back to normal on the canary hosts we rolled: p95 185ms, KV hit 91%. But we still have a fleet with the bad build — need a rollout/kill plan.

ravi: plan: 1) jen to open tokenizer regression PR + test vectors (multilang edgecases) 2) sarah to add kernel-selector assertion + safe-fallback in runtime (small change, revertable) 3) alex to run fleet-wide canary and collect perf histograms across locales 4) I’ll open incident page and notify customers. Target: mitigate within 3 hours.

jen: PR created: https://git.redwood/dev/tokenizer/merge_requests/582 — adds normalizer unit tests for zh/ja/emoji combos and a CI token-count check.

sarah: draft runtime patch: ```yaml
runtime:
  kernel_selector:
    safety_asserts: true
    fallback_policy: force_large_seq_if_mismatch
    logging: tokenization_mismatch
```

sarah: also proposing we temporarily disable ALiBi-variant fallback for qwen2.5 until we confirm RoPE scaling invariants. ALiBi introduced an alternate position mapping that's complicating fallback correctness.

alex: perf after runtime-safety patch on canary: p95 192ms, KV hit 89%. Slight overhead from assertions but acceptable. Will schedule bisect on tokenizer to find offending commit range (likely between commits 1a2b..1f3c).

ravi: good. if bisect points to tokenizer change, we revert that and then re-enable optimized kernel routing. If it's kernel change, we roll that back and add more unit tests. Keep updates in this thread.

jen: adding more test vectors now, will run against whole model matrix (qwen, qwen2, qwen2.5) and will include RoPE scale boundary tests (e.g., sequences around 128/256/512).

alex: FYI for postmortem: include kernel-selection matrix, tokenizer normalization diff, KV packing layout doc, and benchmark tables per locale. Also capture perf-regression delta per commit.

ravi: thanks everyone — update in 30m or sooner if we get a smoking-gun. :thumbsup:
